chunk_findings.detail: The doc text lists `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py` under "Not in the default, add them when they bite", but the same knob's default factory already contains `tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py` and `tests/test_uc_surf_loop_transcript.py`, both of which are matched by that pattern. So the documentation contradictorily presents an already-defaulted pattern as a not-in-default candidate: a user running `ddflow config --explain ci.always_tests` (or reading the knob list) is told to add a glob that is already covered by two explicit default entries, which misstates what "the default" contains and makes the guidance in that sentence unreliable for the other entries in the same list (`tests/test_architecture_guards.py`, `tests/test_compat*.py`). The concrete input demonstrating it is the default value itself: `tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py` ∈ factory default AND matches the pattern advertised as "not in the default".

chunk_findings.detail: The loop reassigns `p` on every iteration, so `p.elapsed_s` on iteration *i* is only the elapsed time of iteration *i-1* — the elapsed time of the pre-hook result that was passed into the function (and of any command before the immediately preceding one) is dropped from the budget arithmetic. The comment still says "what is left", but it is no longer what is left. Concrete case: the pre-hook run (the `p` argument) took 200 s, `budget` is 600 s, and the always command takes 300 s. The first scope command correctly gets `max(min(600,60), 600-200)=400` s, but the selected-tests command is now given `max(min(600,60), 600-300)=300` s instead of `600-500=100` s. The gate can therefore consume 200+300+300 = 800 s of a 600 s budget before the runner's own timeout fires, i.e. the pass/fail threshold of the gate silently moves further out the more "always" commands are configured. Fix by accumulating elapsed time (e.g. keep a running `spent` seeded with the incoming `p.elapsed_s` and subtracting that).

chunk_findings.detail: When the always command fails (or is unavailable), the loop breaks and `p` is that always-command result, so the *only* check emitted is `selected tests (N + M always): False`. The selected tests never ran, yet the gate evidence asserts a selected-tests failure, and there is no separate `always` entry — which is exactly what the stated intent requires ("recorded in the gate evidence as 'always'"). Input: an `[ci].always_tests` guard such as `tests/test_constants_ratchet.py` failing on an unclassified constant; the operator/merge-pipe reading the gate result sees "selected tests failed" and no indication that the always guard, not the selection, is what broke, so the evidence cannot be used to route the fix.

chunk_findings.detail: The old code had a deliberate vacuous-pass safeguard: `if not paths: return Plan("full", "no test reaches the change (running none would pass vacuously)")`. The change weakens it to `if not paths and not always`, so the full-suite fallback only fires when *both* the selection and the always set are empty. In practice `always_tests()` returns the default guard files (`tests/test_constants_ratchet.py`, the layering/transcript/readme/tool-budget globs, plus any file containing `ALWAYS = True`), which exist, so `always` is non-empty for essentially every run. Input that demonstrates it: change a standalone `.py` file (not config/unknown, so `_infrastructure` does not force full) that no test imports — the selector yields `paths == []`, `always` is the non-empty guard list, the function now returns `Plan("selected", …)` whose `commands()` is `[always_command]` and runs only the guard files. Previously this exact input ran the whole suite; now a regression in the changed file can pass the gate with only the repo-wide guards having run, which is precisely the "running none would pass vacuously" case the guard exists to prevent. If this reduction is intended it should be stated explicitly, since it removes the safety net for empty-closure changes.

chunk_findings.detail: The help text added to the golden snapshot says: "Not in the default, add them when they bite: `tests/test_architecture_guards.py` (18 s), `tests/test_compat*.py`, `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py`". chunk_findings.detail:
The shipped default value for `ci.always_tests` is
`["tests/test_constants_ratchet.py", "tests/test_layering*.py", "tests/golden/**", "tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py", "tests/test_uc_surf_loop_transcript.py", "tests/test_readme_*.py", "tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py"]`,
i.e. it *does* include two files that match `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py`. The same knob's doc string then tells the reader "Not in the default, add them when they bite: … `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py`". The two statements cannot both be true of the shipped default, and the practical consequence is the failure mode this change exists to close: a user (or a future maintainer) who reads that the transcript glob is not in the default will not add it, so a newly added `tests/test_uc_surf_<something>_transcript.py` — a repo-wide guard whose input is the whole code base — silently escapes the always set for every selected-scope `ci run`, exactly as `test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript` and `test_uc_surf_loop_transcript` escaped it before (B116c3f2bc8). Either the default should carry the `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py` glob (as the intent's "the transcript tests" implies), or the "not in the default" list must not name a pattern already covered by it.

chunk_findings.detail: The test picks the *first* directory on `PATH` that ends with the string `"/bin"`, writes a `pytest` shell script there (`write_text`, i.e. it overwrites any existing file), makes it executable and never restores it. `endswith("/bin")` is not a marker of the test fixture's shim directory — it is satisfied by every ordinary bin directory. Given a normal developer/CI `PATH` such as `[REDACTED:path]`, and an activated virtualenv (`.../.venv/bin`) also ending in `/bin`, the first match can easily be a *real* bin directory that already contains `pytest` (or the venv's own pytest) rather than the temp stub dir the fixture creates. The concrete consequences: in a read-only system bin the test dies with `PermissionError` (EACCES) instead of exercising the guard; in a writable one (`[REDACTED:path]`, the venv's `bin`) the real `pytest` executable is silently replaced by a shim that exits 1 on any command whose arguments mention `ratchet` and is left in place after the test, so every later subprocess invocation of `pytest` in the same run — and in the developer's shell afterwards — is poisoned, while the test itself still appears to "pass" because the ratchet command fails either way. The test only works in the exact environment where the fixture's own stub directory is the first `/bin`-suffixed entry, so it is not portable across environments (e.g. when the fixture's dir is named anything other than `.../bin`).

The new `always_tests` text reads "...when the closure is empty they run alone, in place of the whole-suite fallback (the guards are the recall for such a change)", and that is what the code does (`ci_scope.plan()` returns the full-suite plan only `if not paths and not always`, and `always_tests()` is non-empty by default). But the unchanged `ci.tests_scope` block in the same dump still tells the reader: "selected (default) runs ... and runs the whole suite instead when the selector says so (a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, **or no test reaches the change**)". "No test reaches the change" is exactly the empty-closure case that `always_tests` now claims no longer falls back to the whole suite — so a user reading `ddflow config --explain` (the input that produces this pinned transcript) gets two mutually exclusive statements about the same case for the shipped default config, and the `tests_scope` one is the false one after this change. The diff updated the `always_tests` sentence but left the neighbouring `tests_scope` sentence asserting the old behaviour; the golden pin should carry one consistent description (either scope out the case in `tests_scope`, e.g. "no test reaches the change *and no always_tests match*", or drop the fallback claim from `always_tests`).

chunk_findings.detail: The test picks the *first* directory on `PATH` that ends with the string `"/bin"`, writes a `pytest` shell script there (`write_text`, i.e. it overwrites any existing file), makes it executable and never restores it. `endswith("/bin")` is not a marker of the test fixture's shim directory — it is satisfied by every ordinary bin directory. Given a normal developer/CI `PATH` such as `[REDACTED:path]`, and an activated virtualenv (`.../.venv/bin`) also ending in `/bin`, the first match can easily be a *real* bin directory that already contains `pytest` (or the venv's own pytest) rather than the temp stub dir the fixture creates. chunk_findings.detail: The change rewrites the whole-suite fallback trigger from "no test reaches the change" to "neither a test nor an `always_tests` file to run". Because the default `always_tests` set is non-empty and its globs (`tests/test_layering*.py`, `tests/golden/**`, the two transcript tests, `tests/test_readme_*.py`, `tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py`, `tests/test_constants_ratchet.py`) always resolve to real files in the repo, the selection can never be empty once the default is in effect. So the fallback for an unreachable change is effectively dead: any change whose file is a normal `.py` file, is not a hub/conftest/pyproject/pre-commit file, and is not in any test's import closure now runs only the fixed guard set instead of the whole suite. For example, a commit that adds `ddflow/tool_main.py` (referenced only from packaging/entry-point metadata or invoked as a subprocess, never imported by a test) previously tripped "no test reaches the change" and ran the whole suite, which executes `tests/test_*_cli_subprocess.py` and catches the failure; with this change the selector reports at least one `always_tests` match, the fallback does not fire, the subprocess test is neither reached nor in `always_tests`, the gate records scope "selected" and passes — exactly the repo-wide failure the change was motivated by (B116c3f2bc8, Bf2d9dab93c). The intent only asks for the always set to run "in addition to the selection"; it does not ask to remove the existing full-suite fallback for changes nothing reaches, and the always globs are a fixed list that by construction cannot cover an arbitrary unreachable source file.

With the shipped non-empty default this removes the whole-suite fallback for a selected-scope run: a diff that no test reaches — e.g. editing `scripts/ci/pre-push`, a shell/template asset, or any non-Python file that the import walk cannot map — now runs only the ~30 s guard set rather than the full suite. The same doc concedes the guard set is not the repository's whole set of repo-wide guards: it deliberately leaves out `tests/test_architecture_guards.py`, `tests/test_compat*.py` and `tests/test_uc_surf_registry_rule_transcript.py` precisely because "their input is the whole code base, so no import closure can know a change affects them" — the identical argument applies to an empty closure, yet those guards are not run there either. So a change that breaks, say, `test_architecture_guards` on an unreachable diff now passes the selected-scope ci and lands on main, which is exactly the class of failure (main red on tests the gate never ran) this change exists to prevent. The stated intent was for the always set to run "in addition to the selection", not to replace the whole-suite fallback; if the fallback is instead meant to stay, then this doc (and the pinned `ci.tests_scope` contract users read) is wrong in the opposite direction.

chunk_findings.detail: The updated `ci.tests_scope` paragraph now says the whole suite is run "when the selector says so (a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, or no test reaches the change)". The removed text for the same sentence had a narrower condition: "…an unknown file type, or neither a test nor an `always_tests` file to run". That exception is exactly what the new knob in this same hunk depends on: the added `ci.always_tests` paragraph promises that the globbed guard tests run for every item in addition to the item's selection, and that when the import closure is empty they run **alone, in place of the whole-suite fallback** ("the guards are the recall for such a change"). Given the input this whole change exists for — a merge whose diff reaches no test (e.g. a regenerated config/pin) — the two paragraphs in the same recorded output now state opposite outcomes: `ci.tests_scope` says the whole suite runs, `ci.always_tests` says only the always set runs instead of it. Either the always set is bypassed precisely when it matters (re-introducing the bug B116c3f2bc8/Bf2d9dab93c failure this change is meant to close), or the fallback described in `ci.tests_scope` never fires; since this file is a golden `--explain` transcript, one of the two recorded sentences is also wrong about the code's actual docstring and will not match the regenerated output. chunk_findings.detail: The change does not merely add the `always_tests` set "in addition to the selection" as the intent describes; it also rewrites the selector's fallback so that the whole suite now runs only when *"neither a test nor an `always_tests` file to run"*, and the `always_tests` doc spells out the consequence: *"when the closure is empty they run alone, in place of the whole-suite fallback (the guards are the recall for such a change)"*. Concrete failure: with the shipped default (non-empty), take a change whose closure is empty because its only exercisers are tests that are deliberately *not* in the default set — the doc's own omissions `tests/test_uc_surf_registry_rule_transcript.py`, `tests/test_compat*.py`, `tests/test_architecture_guards.py`, i.e. exactly the subprocess/whole-repo tests whose "input is the whole code base, so no import closure can know a change affects them". Before this change the selector's conservative rule kicked in and the full suite ran, so that transcript/guard test executed and could catch the regression; after this change the run collapses to the ~7 always files, the omitted test is silently skipped, and the same class of leak the intent cites (B116c3f2bc8 / Bf2d9dab93c: main fails tests the selected-scope gate never ran) is reintroduced for the very tests the doc admits the closure cannot see. The hand-wave "the guards are the recall" does not hold: a fixed 7-file list cannot substitute for the full suite that the pre-existing `no test reaches the change` rule guaranteed. This is an unrequested behaviour change (the intent only asks the always set to run *in addition* to the selection) and it reduces recall by default, not only when a user opts in.

chunk_findings.detail: The new two-stage loop breaks out as soon as the *selected* stage is not ok (`if not scope.ok[label] or at == len(todo) - 1: break`), so the `"always"` stage only ever executes when the selected tests pass. Concrete input: a commit that (a) breaks one selected-scope test and (b) adds an unclassified constant. `todo` is `[(scope.command, "selected"), (scope.always_command, "always")]`; at `at == 0` the selected run fails, `scope.ok["selected"]` is False, the loop breaks, and `scope.always_command` (which would have run `tests/test_constants_ratchet.py`) is never invoked. In `_result`, the check loop only appends labels present in `scope.ok`, so the gate evidence contains a `selected tests (...)` entry and *no* `always` entry at all — the always result was neither run nor recorded, contradicting the stated contract that the always set runs "on every item in addition to the selection" and is "recorded in the gate evidence as 'always'". The developer then fixes the selected failure, re-runs, and only on the second pass discovers the repo-wide ratchet/transcript breakage — exactly the extra merge-fix cycle the change was meant to remove. The loop should run the always stage unconditionally (and record its own `ok`), or at minimum still execute it after a selected-stage failure.

chunk_findings.detail:
The change widens the "selected" case at the expense of the empty-closure fallback. Before, when the import closure reached no test (`paths == []`) the planner deliberately escalated to `Plan("full", "no test reaches the change (running none would pass vacuously)")`, because a selector based on static imports cannot see tests that exercise a file through `importlib`, a subprocess, a fixture that reads the path at runtime, etc. Now that condition is `if not paths and not always`, and `always` is essentially never empty (the defaults match `tests/test_constants_ratchet.py`, `tests/test_layering*.py`, the transcript tests, and any file containing `ALWAYS = True`). So the fallback is now dead in practice.

Concrete input: an item that adds `ddflow/services/newthing.py` which nothing imports yet (or is only reached via a string/dynamic import, e.g. invoked by `ddflow/cli.py` in a subprocess test). The closure is empty, `always` is non-empty, so the planner no longer returns `full`; it returns `Plan("selected", why, "", TESTS_HOOKS, [], cut, sel.cut_at, always, always_cmd)` and only the always guards run. A failing test outside both the always set and the static closure (the subprocess/CLI test that actually drives `newthing.py`) is never executed, so the gate goes green on a change that the previous code would have failed. The intent describes the always set as running "in addition to the selection"; nowhere does it say the empty-selection escalation to the full suite should be dropped — and the vacuous-pass reasoning in the old comment still applies, since the always guards are a tiny subset of the suite, not a replacement for it.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewrite changes the trigger for the whole-suite fallback from "no test reaches the change" to "neither a test nor an `always_tests` file to run". Because `always_tests` has a non-empty default (`tests/test_constants_ratchet.py`, `tests/test_layering*.py`, `tests/golden/**`, the two transcript tests, `tests/test_readme_*.py`, `tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py` — also written verbatim into `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.ci.always_tests.toml`), the predicate "an `always_tests` file to run" is now true for every item. Concrete input: a commit that adds a new module not imported by any test (closure empty) — e.g. `ddflow/newmod.py` with no test reaching it. Previously the selector returned no tests and the gate ran `--full`; with this change the gate runs only the seven guard/pin files and skips the whole suite, so a trivially broken consumer of `newmod.py` passes the selected-scope gate that used to catch it. The intent is explicit that the always set is run "in addition to the selection", not "in place of the whole-suite fallback", so the empty-closure recall net is silently dropped by the shipped default. This also makes the template's `impact = "additive"` wrong: the change does not merely add test runs, it removes the full-suite fallback whenever the config is non-empty.

chunk_findings.detail: This hunk rewrites the fallback contract of the two knobs so that an empty selection now means "run the whole suite": `tests_scope`'s trigger list becomes "… or no test reaches the change", and the `always_tests` doc is changed from "when the closure is empty they run alone, in place of the whole-suite fallback (the guards are the recall for such a change)" to "an empty closure still runs the whole suite (which holds them)". But the `always_tests` docstring still ends with "Empty list: only the selection (and any `ALWAYS = True` file) runs.", which was only true under the old rule (empty closure + non-empty `always_tests` ⇒ guards alone; empty closure + empty list ⇒ fallback). With the new wording those two sentences in the same string cannot both hold: for the input `[ci].always_tests = []` plus a change that no test imports (a private module that is not a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, or an unknown file type), `ci.py:48` promises the whole suite while `ci.py:62` promises only the selection (and `ALWAYS = True` files). Whichever the code does, one of the two documented contracts is now wrong, and the removal of the "guards are the recall for such a change" clause is precisely the recall the change's own evidence (B116c3f2bc8/Bf2d9dab93c: a repo-wide guard test that the selection never ran) asks for — the stated intent only asks for the always-set to run *in addition to* the selection ("they are cheap relative to the full suite: measure and report the seconds"), it says nothing about replacing that guard-only recall with a full-suite run. The `always_tests` doc clause must be updated (or the fallback reverted) so the two knob docs agree.

chunk_findings.detail: The new early return `if not paths: return Plan("full", ...)` makes every item whose change reaches no test file run the *entire* suite, replacing the guard-only fallback that existed before (`if not paths and not always: return Plan("full", ...)` + `cmd = run_command(...) if paths else ""`), which is the only behavioural delta in this hunk. Concrete trigger: a change to a file that no test imports (e.g. adding `assets/logo.svg`, a new data/`.md` file outside every test's import closure) — `sel.tests` is empty, so the function now returns `Plan("full", ...)` and never computes `always`/`always_cmd`. This contradicts the stated intent on two points: (1) the intent's whole rationale is that the always set is "cheap relative to the full suite" and that guard tests are the recall for changes the closure cannot map, yet those exact items now pay for the whole suite, defeating the economy the change is supposed to preserve; (2) the intent requires the always set to be "recorded in the gate evidence as 'always'" (count, files, `always_s`), but with scope `full` the always files are never recorded/measured as `always` for these items. It is also the only case where the run can lose recall rather than gain it: `always_tests` is user-configurable and can name a guard the default suite would not collect (e.g. a file outside `testpaths`, or one only run when invoked by path), and here the full-suite plan silently drops the explicit `always` invocation, which is the same failure mode as B116c3f2bc8. The removal of the previous documented behaviour is masked by the simultaneous golden-snapshot edit (`tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr`, "an empty closure still runs the whole suite"), which rewrites the expectation to match the new code rather than reflecting the intent.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten test asserts `res.scope["scope"] == "full"` and then `assert not _calls(stubs, "pytest")`, i.e. it encodes that on an empty closure the tool itself invokes nothing and the guard/transcript/pin tests are only run if some *external* hook reruns the full suite. That removes the observable guarantee the previous version of this test provided (it asserted the always-set file `tests/test_readme_table.py` was actually handed to pytest when the closure was empty). Concretely: given input `{"notes/memo.md": "hi\n"}` (a doc/constant change that no test imports), the test now passes even if zero tests execute at all — even if the caller does not run the "unmodified hook". That is exactly the B116c3f2bc8/Bf2d9dab93c failure mode the change is supposed to close (a green gate that ran no guards), now re-asserted as expected behaviour rather than caught: an environment that invokes the selected-scope CI directly (CI job / CLI / agent call, not via the pre-commit hook) returns "full", runs no pytest, and the guard, pin and transcript tests never run. The test should either assert the always set is still executed (or that the full suite is actually executed by the caller), not assert the absence of any test run.
